name: Alphabet Inc.
window: Q1 FY26 · Apr 29 → Jul 28, 2026 (through the 07-22 print)

events.text: Consolidated revenue $109.9B, +22% (+19% cc); OI +30% to $39.7B, margin 36.1%; EPS $5.11 (+82%, inflated by equity gains). Search & Other +19% to $60.4B (fastest in ~5 years). Google Cloud +63% to $20B (first time >$20B), OI tripled to $6.6B, margin 32.9%; backlog ~doubled q/q to $462B, now including TPU hardware sales. Capex $35.7B; FY26 guide raised to $180-190B; C27 to 'increase significantly'.

Search +16% XFX / +19% reported (better than the buy-side 'high-teens' bar); Google Cloud +60%+; Gemini model revenue +800% y/y; AI Max now ~30% of campaigns; the print pulled '27 EPS estimates 'much closer to $15'.

Accounting clarification: Google books external TPU hardware sales on a GROSS basis, with a license-fee markup of ~10-15% (~$2-3K/chip), the full value in the Cloud backlog (no capex). ~$85B of TPU dollars entered the 1Q26 backlog (vs ~$11.5B in 4Q25), reflecting ~4GW of Anthropic orders; ex-TPU leaves ~$365B of 'pure' backlog. First quarter without a buyback since COVID; TPU revenue recognition mostly a 2027 event.

PT $450, owned/liked; Q1 pulled forward a positive revision cycle: ~30%+ cloud revenue revision in C27/28, mid-teens consolidated OI revision; ~$14 GAAP EPS '27 / ~$17 '28 (buy-side whisper $15+/$17.50-18+); sum-of-parts >$450.

'Best asset on Earth', won the AI Game of Thrones — the TPU bull case is now the base case, cloud guided to 80-90% growth over the next ~7 quarters by the backlog book. But bear: ranks GOOG #3 of the MAG (Meta>Amazon>Google): 'hard to re-rate Google five turns on a $5T cap', no near-term dry powder for multiple expansion.

The ~500MW-class Google/Blackstone DC vehicle for TPUs is read as a financing structure for TPU capex (not Google OEM'ing chips); ~80-90% of TPU inference is for Google's own properties (Search/YouTube/AI Mode) — Google Cloud probably runs more GPUs than TPUs; a ratio of one Axion CPU to two TPUs.
Buy $447 based on AI Search ad formats.
OW $405; AI Search = 'biggest change in 25 years', with higher CTR/coverage.

Flags 'anti-gravity' (agentic app building) as a dormant 'killer app' — an Atlassian reseller reportedly replaced its Salesforce CRM with it; framed alongside GCP's best-in-class Q1 backlog and quantum as underappreciated next catalysts.
The $85B raise = 'Mag7 morphing from cash machines into capital-intensive giants — weighs on multiples regardless of the top-line'.
C27 capex revised to ~$300B (MS, +57% y/y, Altimeter data); FCF only $10.1B in Q1, buybacks shrinking, depreciation accelerating.

At WWDC 2026 Apple gave Gemini a dedicated keynote slide as the foundation anchoring Siri/Apple Intelligence with world knowledge (replacing the prior bolt-on ChatGPT framing); Counterpoint reads Google deeper into agentic experiences. Google One AI now includes a new $100/month plan reserving the latest Gemini features.

Processing ~3.2 quadrillion tokens/month (~7x y/y) — evidence that agentic inference is the marginal unit of compute demand. JPM models capex FY26 $185B, ~$300B FY27E / ~$350B FY28E; FCF compresses to ~$12B FY26E → -$27B FY27E. Funding: ~$51bn of senior notes YTD + an $84.75bn equity raise; 'crossed the Rubicon' to a structural funding requirement. TPU units 1.8M (2025) → 4.5M (2026E) → 8.0M (2027E).

Search demand re-accelerating through 2026 after the April-war wobble — Legg models Search Q2 27% / Q4 +25% (raised +3pts), FY ~26%, with AI Max made mandatory for large advertisers from September (~1pt tailwind) + the first Gemini ad; YouTube re-accelerating (FY ~21%) on B2B.

Gemini co-lead Noam Shazeer leaving for OpenAI (<2 years after the $2.7B Character.AI deal) — a near-term overhang at DeepMind. Maintains Buy. (Samsung foundry engagement for Axion and TPU v10 'Icefish' work also cited.)

Rising HBM cost is the driver of Google's shift to MediaTek (Broadcom charges HBM in the BOM, MediaTek does not); MediaTek's procurement share rising from 6%→30% (2026-28). Google tried to buy HBM directly but found it too challenging, so procurement stays split between Broadcom and MediaTek for ~3 years.

Strong Google TPU demand acceleration — over the past ~3 months Google has been asking aggressively for TSMC wafer capacity + CoWoS allocation, the demand engine behind GS raising 2027/28 CoWoS + MediaTek Google-TPU ASIC estimates (MediaTek 2027E to ~US$20bn).

'DC Capex Ramping to >$1.4T in 2028E' — GOOGL saw the HIGHEST hyperscaler capex revision, +83%/101% '27/'28, driven by expanding TPU deployments + external-sales aspirations. Sits inside Mizuho's frame: AI DC capex $1.2T'27/>$1.4T'28; hyperscaler-only $846B/$912B '27/'28 (up 54%/66% off YE-25 cons).

GOOGL adds the most compute capacity of the group — 9 GW/11 GW in '27/'28 (reaching ~31 GW available compute by '28, #2 behind AWS ~35 GW), with hyperscale (Cloud/TPU) revs 'set to accelerate with strong profitability'; ~3 GW sold external. Inside the ~$1.2t/$1.4t '27/'28 sector frame (4x compute to ~120 GW by '28); TPU ~20s/watt vs GPU ~$50/watt cost edge.

Maintain BUY, PO $430 (px $357.18). App DAUs: Google +1% m/m 2.2bn, Gemini +7% 118mn, Claude +9% 18mn. Web traffic YoY (Similarweb, June): Google +4% to 2.8bn/day, Gemini +341%, Claude +736% — Google traffic still grows even as AI-natives explode off small bases; 'expansionary moment for Search' = continued 2026 strength.

Reiterates OW, Dec-26 PT $460 (top pick #1). JPMe 2Q26 Search +16.6% / YT +8.6% / Cloud +70.9%; FY26/27/28 rev $492.7B/$604.5B/$735.1B, GAAP EPS $14.05/$14.34/$17.31; capex $185.9B'26 → $293.4B'27 (+54%) → $348.5B'28; FCF $17.9B'26 → –$16.7B'27 → +$7.8B'28. Buyside bars: Search 17%+, Cloud 70%+, EPS'27 $15+, capex'27 $300B+. Cloud 'at least 70' exiting the year in the 80s; still no ads in Gemini (a lever).

events.src: BofA · Justin Post / Nitin Bansal ('2Q Preview: Estimate Change')
events.text: Maintain BUY, PO $430 (px $370.92) — raising estimates into the 07-22 print for Cloud strength (offset slightly by FX). Raises Cloud growth est to 70% (backlog implies ≥$230bn revs over next 8 quarters); expects 2Q rev/EPS $102.1bn/$8.38 (Street $101.0bn), incl. ~$80bn benefit to 2Q OI from the Anthropic-stake revaluation (Anthropic $380bn 1Q → $965bn 2Q). FY26: net rev +1% to $427bn, EPS +36% to $19.70 (16% Search, 72% Cloud growth); FY27 EPS $14.70; FY28 EPS $18.12.

'The Paths to 25-50% GenAI ROIC' — Overweight, PT $400 = ~24x the average of MS's $15/$18 '27/'28 EPS, implying ~1.6x PEG, a ~35% premium to the peer median; bull $450 (~26x ~$16/~$19), bear $225 (~15x ~$14/~$16, 'New AI products create greater than expected margin pressure due to lower monetization rates and increased compute intensity'). Spot $319.74, mean consensus PT $420.48 (range $220-$515), 89% OW; options-implied (24 Jul 2026) P(>$450) ~13.1%, P(>$400) ~23.5%, P(<$225) ~15.3% — the ONLY one of MS's four internet names where the base case is more likely than the bear, which reads the 07-22 drawdown as capex de-rating rather than thesis impairment. The structural point: GOOGL is the only name MS puts on BOTH sides of the framework — bullish 'hyperscalers AMZN, GOOGL, MSFT' AND 'model developers GOOGL and META' — because it runs GCP and Gemini off the same fleet, so it captures the landlord spread (GPU rental at $8.50/hr → $22.9bn revenue/GW, ~67% incremental EBIT margin, ~31% ROIC) AND the tenant spread (model API on owned infrastructure at 2,750 tok/s/GPU and $1.75/mn → $30bn/GW, ~75% margin, ~46% ROIC) on the same gigawatt. The third framework (same API on 3P/rented infra at $7.75/hr → ~31% margin / ~25% NOPAT margin) prices the ~$50/W SpaceX arrangement as a bridge cost. Total GAAP operating income 129,039 (2025) → 176,395 (26e) → 227,461 (27e) → 280,882 (28e), i.e. +36.7% / +29.0% / +23.5% — the sharpest contrast on the complex with META's +3.0% 2028 OI growth on a comparable build. Caveats: reported near-term incremental margins run below the band, and the frameworks are GB300-based — MS explicitly notes custom ASICs have lower cost but also lower chip price/hour and throughput, so these are NOT TPU economics.

Fubon reverses its own 07-08 TPU-v9 packaging call, and the driver is Google's own volume target. Verbatim: 'Despite market concerns on Google's capex and negative FCF, we see Google has a very aggressive target in 2028 to deploy its in-house design TPUs. Based on our checks, Google plans to have 12-15mn TPUs in 2028. Entering 2028, Google's TPUs will enter the V9 generation with four compute dies, suggesting that their capacity consumption will more than double in 2028 vs. 2027... we think it is difficult to reach Google's target with TSMC alone, and Intel's supply is a must by 2028.' Twenty days earlier the same house had concluded Google would 'at last rely on TSMC's [2028 CoWoS] expansion plan' because Intel could not hit the 95%+ EMIB-T yield bar by mid-2027 — the reversal comes from the demand side, not from an improved yield view, since a four-compute-die V9 more than doubles per-unit packaging consumption and the volume simply does not fit inside TSMC's book. On Intel, Fubon is now constructive on capacity if not the learning curve: 'although there is still a lot of noise on Intel's EMIB-T progress, especially its learning curve improvement, we see Intel becoming more positive in capacity expansion' — EMIB capacity 10-12k/month by end-2026, planned to double to 24-25k/month by end-2027, with the CFO earmarking a great portion of new capex for advanced packaging and Ibiden's next call the tell. TSMC baseline for context: CoWoS 180kwpm end-2027 → 220kwpm end-2028 (SoIC 4Q28 cut 90k → 70k to prioritise CoWoS). Two flags kept open: the 12-15mn figure was relayed by the same house on 07-17 as a chip/DIE-basis number, and 12-15mn dies (≈3-4mn packages) is not the same claim as 12-15mn packages (≈48-60mn dies); and Fubon calls the target 'very aggressive' explicitly despite market concern on Google capex and negative FCF — the supply chain building for a plan the equity market has been penalising. MediaTek is Fubon's top TPU pick.

events.src: Goldman Sachs · Eric Sheridan / Gabriela Borges / Jim Schneider
events.text: 'Sizing the AI Economy Needed to Justify ROIC on Hyperscaler AI Capex' — six US hyperscalers need ~$1.42trn of CY2028-30 revenue (~$11.6bn/GW/yr) for a 15% ROIC on ~$1.73trn of Phase-2 (CY26-27) AI capex at ~$42bn/GW, 70/30 compute/shells. GOOGL (85% of GSe total capex): $470.1bn — the largest slice — → 11GW → $385.3bn of CY28-30 revenue required = 77.7% of the $496bn C2Q26 RPO (AMZN 67.7%, MSFT 39.6%). GS records Google's ability to shift capacity between Search/YouTube/DeepMind and Cloud. Buy, PT $435 (unchanged). Google-SpaceX compute licensing deal excluded from the base.

events.src: Goldman Sachs Portfolio Strategy · Ryan Hammond / Ben Snider
events.text: 'AI capex, required revenues, and what's priced in the AI trade' — hyperscaler capex $800bn in 2026, consensus $1.1trn in 2027 (GSe $1.2trn '27 / $1.4trn '28; growth ~100% → 54% → 12%); ~$300bn/yr of AI revenue needed to break even. AMZN/GOOGL/MSFT/ORCL cloud growth 25% (2024) → 48% (Q2 2026), ~$70bn annualised above the 2024 trend; AMZN/GOOGL/MSFT backlog ~$1.7trn. Hyperscalers at their lowest P/E in over a decade. Strategy note, no GOOGL rating.

'AI Summit Recap: Still Early with Demand Outstripping Supply' — GOOGL a top pick with MSFT and AMZN. Expert Bill MacCartney views GOOGL as best positioned for personal AI given ownership of user context across its distribution interface (7 apps with 2B users); AAPL advantaged on trust; consumers likely to use 2-3 primary agents.

events.src: Morgan Stanley · Simeon Gutman / Brian Nowak et al.
events.text: 'Muse: Rewriting the Retail/Consumer Playbook' — search effective take rates estimated 5-10x early agentic offerings; 80%+ of retailer online traffic still unpaid/direct. Sensitivity: a 500bp shift from unpaid to paid traffic offsets a 1,400bp decline in GOOGL's effective take rates, while GOOGL would need ~3,800bp of traffic shift to break even at a 5% take rate — 'the mathematical risk to GOOGL's highly-monetizing search business if they do not lead the agentic transition'. MS expects a better agent around Gemini 4 in 4Q; Carrefour first European food retailer on Google's UCP. GOOGL Overweight, no PT stated.

events.src: Jefferies expert call · Horizon Media digital-media executive
events.text: Capstone call notes — agency digital budgets ~+10% y/y; split 30-35% Google / 30-35% Meta / ~30% diversified; 'concentration in Google and Meta has not moderated whatsoever'. ChatGPT's US audience reach 'significantly smaller than Google, Meta, and even Reddit', spend not material, no outsize returns; LLMs drive brand uplift more than lower-funnel performance.
